questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I wanted to get more fieldwork experience which i could in UNIS. 
Doing fieldwork in the arctic is a good exercise because it is difficult and it requires alot of planning. I am sure these experiences will help me in my future professional carrier.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Everything was given in the introduction lectures or through emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not need any assistance. everything was laid out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Student accomodation is only available through Samskipnaden. If you want to find something outside Samskipnaden it will probably be very difficult and expensive

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Samskipnaden offers a shared kitchen. You dont need to bring anything for cooking. You have to cook yourself, there is no service for dinner.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is nice to share this space with other students, and you will have a good time. Book you housing in very good time. Otherwise you might have to move a-lot around within the student accommodation

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is a bit expensive and Samskipnaden has some weird rules and want to be in control of example if you bring a guest to live with you. Then you have to pay extra fees. This is weird. Its a room you pay for, why would you pay extra to have a friend visiting you??

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Søknadsweb is quit easy to once you figure it out. 

But!, since UNIS is a university you can be enrolled at you have to also apply for another norwegian university such as UiT Tromsø. This can be quit confusing.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You got to søknadsweb and apply for a Norwegian university which u want to be studying though to get into UNIS. You then have to make 2 profiles, one for the host university in norway and then one profile for UNIS. You then have to upload different documents such as your grades, transcripts and passport on both profiles.

Then you wait to be accepted into both universities.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can contact UNIS and UiT. They are both very helpful if you have questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very. I got the courses i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you apply way before the deadline so you are sure to have time enough to handle any problems along the way. Also contact the universities if you have any trouble, they will help you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The programmes offered what was written in the course descriptions.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is up to you. You can follow the courses rather easy and pass. But given the freedom and self chosen topics it is possible to reach quit high academic levels

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Much different. University of Copenhagen is normally rather dense in form of information and theory, but does rarely offer time to apply the skills you learn to anything. UNIS offers also alot of theory but way less than what i would get in University of Copenhagen, instead you have more time to use the skills you learn to actually apply what you learned and create scientific article style reports.

Therefore: University of Copenhagen is good if you want to learn alot of theory fast.
UNIS is great if you want to learn how to make good reports, have time to read scientific papers, learn how to do field work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
AG-211 - Marine Geology
AG-210 - Quarternary Geology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: These are the only courses offered in the fall semester for bachelor geology students. They are great, take them.

questions.answer: If you want to experience svalbard tourism, then expect it to be very expensive. 2000 NOK for a one day trip. Auch, but worth it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
There is a skateboard ramp which i used haha

Hiking is the main activity here.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Non really.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking. There is also a gym.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Most people you will interact with is going to be other students

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Dont be shy. Everyone here is new and so are you. Everyone is excited to go hiking and will probably take you if you ask.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Non

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Every student brings their own culture so you will meet alot of interresting people. Embrace everyone.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go hiking as much as possible. Have fun.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Not really. The town is small. Go explore a bit and see what you find. 
Most useful information is given at the introduction lectures.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Doing fieldwork was the best. Sailing for 5 days straight in the arctic, what else can wish for? Saling 5 days back and forth to a freshly deglaciated forefield and getting to see whales, dolphins, walrus and beautiful geology? Svalbard is a nature heaven.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably trying to keep up with reports. Everyone set the bar really high. Dont let it stress you though.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you decide to come here then you will have a experience of a lifetime. Just sign up already?

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
